environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, MSVC 14.51, vcpkg 65a2c23 (x64-windows), loopback, real time
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
objective: GameNetworkingSockets spike (D-012): build it via vcpkg and measure reliability and default security on loopback.
hypothesis: GNS 1.6.1 gives reliable ordered delivery under loss/lag and encrypted connections out of the box; authentication needs extra setup.
procedure: vcpkg manifest (gamenetworkingsockets, default-features false) -> cmake -S . -B build-gns -DMORDOR_WITH_GNS=ON -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=<vcpkg>/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake; cmake --build build-gns --config Release; ctest --test-dir build-gns -C Release x3 (unit, integration, network, gns).
expected_result: Spike tests pass; security flags recorded as observed.
observed_result: Resolved: GameNetworkingSockets 1.6.1, OpenSSL 3.6.5, protobuf 7.36.2 (protoc 36.2.0), abseil 20260107.1; dependency build took ~12 min (configure 737.7 s). First run: all 3 GNS tests FAILED - GNS refused CreateListenSocketIP with port 0 (debug output: 'Cannot create listen socket. Must specify local port.'); fixed by probing a free loopback port. Then 3/3 passed on 3 ctest runs (with all 52 prototype tests): 2000 reliable messages each way exact and in order; 1000 each way exact and in order under GNS fake 15% loss, 40 ms lag, 5% reorder (ping reported 80 ms). Default security flags on a plain IP connection: unencrypted=0 (encrypted), unauthenticated=1 (NOT authenticated). So GNS alone does not satisfy the WAN authentication prerequisite (KI-04/KI-17) without certificate/identity setup.
errors: First attempt: 'Cannot create listen socket. Must specify local port.' (test bug, fixed)
follow_up: Evaluate GNS authentication options that need no Valve service; implement the Transport interface and run the existing suites and soak against a GNS backend.
